sources.news_title: Trump Admin Declares Total Victory Over Algae Thanks to ‘Advanced Nanobubbler Technology’
Reflecting Pool algae compared to Iranian Navy by Interior Dept as cracks show
sources.text:
THE Interior Department has compared dead algae in Donald Trump’s renovated Reflecting Pool to the destroyed Iranian Navy in a bizarre social media post.
The strange boast came as a tear appeared in the pool’s new blue sealant and “pro-slime” protesters rallied in support of the green bloom.
Three demonstrators staged the tongue-in-cheek rally beside the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, DC.
The tiny group appeared to mock the administration’s frantic effort to remove the green bloom from the famous landmark.
National Park Service crews were still vacuuming dead algae from the bottom of the pool as the protest unfolded.
The spectacle came just days after the water turned green following a renovation costing more than $14 million.
READ MORE ON NEWS
Workers have been battling to restore the “American Flag Blue” color ordered by Trump ahead of America’s 250th birthday.
But new footage raised further questions after chunks of the coating appeared to be lifting from the pool floor.
It was not immediately clear how widespread the apparent damage was or what caused it.
Officials have not publicly confirmed whether the coating has been damaged by the cleanup operation.
Most read in The US Sun
Crews poured jugs marked “12% hydrogen peroxide” into the water on Tuesday as they fought the algae.
The Interior Department said the chemical was milder than chlorine and had “no harmful side effects” for wildlife or the environment.
Officials also deployed a $1.7 million nanobubble treatment system designed to starve and destroy the algae.
The technology pumps ozone-filled microscopic bubbles into the water to break down toxins and other contaminants.
The Interior Department declared on Thursday that the system had “very effectively killed” the bloom.
It said workers were now vacuuming up dead algae that had settled across parts of the pool floor.
“The Reflecting Pool water is crystal clear,” the department claimed.
It said the cleanup was the final maintenance stage and would be finished within days.
Officials also compared the dead algae at the bottom of the pool to destroyed Iranian warships.
The algae was resting there “just like the destroyed Iranian Navy resting on the bottom of the Persian Gulf,” the department posted on X.
The administration said the section closest to the Lincoln Memorial had already been cleared.
Pictures shared by officials showed the blue coating becoming visible again after the algae was removed.
However, algae expert Christopher Gobler warned that the treatments may only provide temporary relief.
“There’s always going to be a rebound of the algae,” the Stony Brook University professor told Reuters.
“Hopefully it works as a quick fix, but these algae do tend to rebound.”
The pool was drained, sealed and resurfaced before refilling began on June 5.
It turned visibly green again within days as temperatures rose across the capital.
The Interior Department blamed “residual” algae left inside supply pipes while the pool was empty.
Officials described the bloom as part of the site’s “normal startup process.”
Trump previously insisted the new surface was far more than a basic coat of paint.
“This was not a paint job,” he wrote on Truth Social on June 5.
“This was highly sophisticated material, industrial strength, that could last for 100 years, applied by very talented people.”
The no-bid resurfacing contract was awarded to Virginia-based Atlantic Industrial Coatings.
Trump has said the company previously carried out work at one of his golf clubs.
The president originally placed the cost of the project at about $1.8 million before it climbed beyond $14 million.
Algae has repeatedly plagued the shallow pool since it opened in 1922.
The landmark stretches between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument and was the setting for Martin Luther King Jr.’s 1963 “I Have a Dream” speech.

sources.news_title: Interior Department compares Reflecting Pool algae to Iran’s navy
Critics torch Interior’s Trump-coded 'propaganda' post on algae-plagued project
sources.text:
Online critics are blasting U.S. Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum’s press team for politicizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool by comparing now-dead algae, which reached five-year-high levels, to the remnants of the Iranian Navy — all while taking a swipe at President Barack Obama.
According to The Washington Post on Thursday, Reflecting Pool algae has “roared back,” reaching the “highest levels in years.”
 “President Donald Trump vowed in April to clean up what he called the ‘filthy’ and ‘disgusting’ water in the Reflecting Pool,” the Post reported. “He promised to resurface the basin to eliminate persistent leaking and to paint it ‘American flag blue.’ Once the pool started to be refilled, on June 4, he praised its ‘clean, beautiful water.'”
 “An analysis of satellite imagery of the Lincoln Memorial shows algae levels spiked days after a $14 million renovation was completed,” the Post noted.
But not according to the Interior Department, which declared hours earlier, late Wednesday night, that the algae problem had been eliminated — just like the Iranian Navy.
 “The Reflecting Pool water is crystal clear, and our National Park Service team is now vacuuming up the dead algae resting on the bottom of some parts of the Reflecting Pool—just like the destroyed Iranian Navy resting on the bottom of the Persian Gulf,” an Interior Department social media post declared.
Interior did not stop there.
“Previous administrations—most notably under Obama—failed to maintain the Reflecting Pool, and after refilling the pool, the water would quickly become murky and thick with massive clumps of algae floating on the surface,” it said, before attacking the media as well.
 “As our National Park Service team noted, the Reflecting Pool is now so ‘blue’ that the Fake News Media, which has been staked out at the Reflecting Pool for weeks, has fled!”
Online critics blasted Interior’s post.
“Why the hell is my government’s interior press account making jabs at foreign affairs? FFS, yall supposed to be adults, and you’re acting like petulant children,” wrote one critic. “‘Funny’ is not something I want from my administration. I want resolutions. I want fixes. They are more obsessed with social media & making good clips than making our lives affordable, our wages higher, giving us healthcare.”
“Americans died in this war,” noted communications strategist and political analyst Melik Abdul. “Please stop disrespecting them by comparing the circumstances surrounding their deaths to vacuuming algae. Stick with what you do best and leave your military fantasies out of it. It’s lazy and childish.”
 “What purpose does lying serve America?” asked another critic. “Anyone can view the live feed, and see the pool is still green and very much NOT clear. The entire pool is still green, with a couple tiny spots clear, but refilling with Algae as noted from two days ago to this morning the entire edge is refilled with green.”
“Comparing the algae in the reflecting pool after its $14.2 million fraud, waste, and abuse paint job to Iran’s navy isn’t the flex the Department of Interior seems to think it is,” wrote U.S. Air Force Colonel (Ret.) Moe Davis.
“This is an actual U.S. government account spewing deceptive propaganda comparing Trump’s failed Reflecting Pool renovation to his failed Iran War and Memorandum of Understanding,” wrote another critic.
Not all remarks were critical. U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R-WI) responded to the Interior Dept.’s post by writing: “This warms my heart.”

sources.news_title: Trump team labels algae cleanup from the Reflecting Pool a ‘national priority’
sources.text:
Trump team labels cleaning algae from the Reflecting Pool a ‘regional and national priority’ ahead of July 4
National Park Service employees reportedly received an email urging them to support ‘critical pre-July 4th operational needs,’ including ‘scrubbing and pump out operations’
The Trump administration has labeled the algae cleanup operation in the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool a “regional and national priority” in an email to staff, urging them to work overtime to scrub the monument in time for July 4 celebrations, according to a report.
President Donald Trump’s $14 million pet project to resurface the 2,000-foot pool, which was supposed to make the water appear an “American flag blue,” has turned green after becoming infested with algae just days after completion.
National Park Service employees received an email, obtained by MeidasTouch, urging them to support “critical pre-July 4th operational needs” at the Reflecting Pool, according to the outlet.
Crews are required to help with “scrubbing and pump out operations” at the Washington, D.C. landmark and are being asked to work 12-hour shifts beginning this week in a bid to rid the pool of algae, the outlet reports.
The Interior Department, which oversees the National Park Service, confirmed that the Trump administration was calling in reinforcements for the cleanup in a statement to The Independent.
“Unlike the Obama and Biden administrations that shamefully chose to let our national treasures descend into filth and disrepair, the Trump administration is marshaling in the necessary resources to ensure the capital city of the most powerful country in the world is absolutely stunning in honor of our historic 250th celebrations,” a spokesperson said. “It is beyond comprehension why anyone would be upset that President Trump is making D.C. Safe and Beautiful Again.”
In a previous statement, a spokesperson told The Independent that the department is deploying nanobubble ozone technology to blitz the algae.
“This technology is actively killing algae, pathogens (e.g., E. coli), and contaminants that have long plagued the Reflecting Pool since 1922, most infamously, the Obama pool reopening that resulted in massive algae clumps taking over the pool’s surface following years of construction that cost,” the spokesperson said.
While algae has been a persistent problem in the Reflecting Pool, the current levels have reached the highest in years, according to The Washington Post. In fact, days after Trump’s renovation was completed, the pool had more algae in it than at any point in the month of June for at least five years, according to the newspaper, which requested specialized analysis of satellite data from experts.
Alana Menendez, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Virginia’s Department of Environmental Sciences, analyzed satellite data which detected more algae in the pool in an image taken a week after it reopened “than in any June images going back to 2021.”
The researcher analysed data from a European satellite that captures images of the Reflecting Pool several times a month. The images can be used to determine an estimate of the presence of chlorophyll, the green pigment found in algae, in the water.
The level of algae from the data was among the highest measured in any month in the past two years, the analysis found.
Menendez told the newspaper that it was not unusual for higher levels of algae to exist in the months of June due to more sunlight and higher temperatures than in the winter months.
The White House touted the nanobubble technology to “keep the Reflecting Pool crystal clear” in a statement to the newspaper. “Thanks to President Trump, new lining and industrial grade materials will permanently seal the Reflecting Pool, which previously leaked 16 million gallons per year and wasted countless taxpayer dollars,” spokesman Taylor Rogers said.
This week, workers outfitted in neon vests were seen dumping hydrogen peroxide into the pool. Photos showed crews unloading numerous large boxes — apparently filled with the cleaning solution — at multiple points along the pool’s perimeter.
The Interior Department said the chemical was a “milder treatment than chlorine,” which has “no harmful side effects to marine life or to the environment.”

sources.news_title: Trump admin compares reflecting pool cleanup to Iranian Navy’s destruction
sources.text:
The Trump administration compared a cleanup of algae in Washington, D.C.’s Reflecting Pool to the destruction of Iran’s navy, an unusual analogy pairing a routine maintenance project with a serious and deadly military conflict.
The comparison came in a post Wednesday by the Interior Department on X, which promoted new technology used to treat the water and described the pool as “crystal clear.”
“Advanced nanobubbler technology very effectively killed the algae that has plagued every Lincoln Reflecting Pool reopening—most infamously Obama’s reopening—since 1922,” the post said.
But recent images suggest a more mixed picture.
A current aerial view of the Reflecting Pool, a central feature of the National Mall stretching between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument, shows the water still appearing green, suggesting the cleanup effort may be ongoing or uneven despite the administration’s characterization.
Fighting Algae vs. Fighting Iran
It was the language used to describe that final stage of the cleanup that stood out.
According to the post, workers are vacuuming up algae “resting on the bottom of some parts of the Reflecting Pool—just like the destroyed Iranian Navy resting on the bottom of the Persian Gulf.”
The comparison marked a notable departure from the typically technical tone of updates about maintenance work on federal landmarks, introducing a pointed geopolitical reference into what is usually a routine operational update.
Republican congressmen reacted positively to the statement online, with Wisconsin Representative Derrick Van Orden saying it "warms" his heart, and Utah Representative Burgess Owens quoting the post with a series of celebratory emojis.
The statement came the same day President Donald Trump signed a memorandum of understanding with Iran aimed at ending the conflict between the two countries, an agreement that includes a ceasefire framework and sets the stage for further negotiations toward a broader peace deal.
At least 13 U.S. service members have been killed and hundreds more wounded, according to Pentagon-linked figures, while across the region the death toll runs into the thousands, with the majority of casualties reported in Iran and neighboring countries hit by the fighting.
Iran’s naval forces, meanwhile, have suffered significant damage, with U.S. officials claiming dozens of vessels destroyed and independent reporting confirming multiple ships sunk or disabled. But analysts say the navy has not been wiped out entirely, with smaller craft, submarines and coastal defenses still intact.
What Is Nanoblubber Technology?
The Reflecting Pool has long struggled with recurring algae blooms, which can cloud the water and detract from one of Washington’s most recognizable sites. Federal officials have for years tested a range of methods to address the issue, including upgrades to filtration and circulation systems.
The “nanobubbler” system referenced in the Interior Department’s post works by injecting microscopic air bubbles into the water, increasing oxygen levels and disrupting the conditions that allow algae to thrive.
The Reflecting Pool, which stretches between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument, attracts millions of visitors each year. For now, officials say its water is among the clearest it has been in recent memory—even as the administration’s phrasing ensures the cleanup effort is receiving attention for more than just the results.
Update, 06/18/2026, 10:57 a.m. ET: This article was updated with additional information.
